title: Turn ideas into one test
author: Visual Slides

slides.title: Turn ideas into one test
slides.subtitle: Help a team leave an idea workshop with a question it can answer.
slides.body_html: Group ideas around the need they address, then pick an uncertainty and plan a small test.
slides.notes_en: A workshop can produce a lot of ideas. The useful outcome is knowing which question to answer next. Here is a short sequence to get there.
slides.notes_zh: 让工作坊产出可验证的问题
slides.background_alt: Illustrative photo: a team placing sticky notes on a wall

slides.title: Group ideas by the need they serve
slides.subtitle: Ask what people need to do before comparing particular interface changes.
slides.body_html:
Example

How can people tell a change was saved?

A confirmation message and a status indicator belong together if they address the same need. Give the group a name that describes that need.

Use the group to choose which idea to explore and explain what the other ideas have in common.
slides.notes_en: Two ideas may look different and still answer the same need. Here a confirmation message and a status indicator both help people check what happened. Grouping them around that shared need makes comparison easier.
slides.notes_zh: 按照用户要完成的事归类

slides.title: Choose the uncertainty to test
slides.subtitle: Write down the need, the open question and the behavior that would help answer it.
slides.body_html: What will you watch for when someone tries it?
slides.notes_en: Write the question so you can answer it by watching a realistic task. In this example, ask a person to save a change and see if they find the result without a prompt. Ask what they think happened.
slides.notes_zh: 把假设写成能观察的行为

backdrop.alt: Illustrative photo: a person testing a website on a laptop

slides.title: Build only what the task requires
slides.subtitle: Make the shortest interaction that lets someone change a setting, save and check the result.
slides.body_html:
Prototype scope

Make saving visible

Start with a setting and a way to save it. Include the confirmation you want to compare.

Observe the next step

Watch where someone looks after saving. Follow up on what they expected to see.
slides.notes_en: We only need the interaction that lets someone change a setting, save and look for a result. Watch what they do before explaining the design. Their response tells us what to adjust in the next draft.
slides.notes_zh: 搭出能验证问题的最小操作

backdrop.alt: Illustrative photo: wireframes sketched on paper

slides.title: Workshop prompts
slides.subtitle: Use these questions when the group needs help moving from ideas to a test.
slides.body_html: <dl class="source-list reveal" style="--delay:190ms"><dt>Group</dt><dd>Which ideas address the same need? How would a participant describe that need?</dd><dt>Choose</dt><dd>What do we need to learn to make a decision? What action would give us an answer?</dd><dt>Scope</dt><dd>Which parts of the idea must work for someone to try the task?</dd><dt>Observe</dt><dd>What did they do? What did they expect? What should we change next?</dd></dl>
slides.source_credit: Visuals in this example are illustrations prepared for the skill.
slides.notes_en: Use these questions to coach a group as they prepare an experiment.
slides.notes_zh: 讨论时可以回到这几个提示
